title: "Structuring Your Application"

# Structuring Your Application

As a command-line tool evolves from a single-file prototype into a multi-command production system, code organization becomes paramount. A well-structured CLI separates argument parsing and terminal presentation from domain business logic.

## Separation of Concerns: The `main.rs` vs `lib.rs` Pattern

Never write all application logic in `main.rs`. Instead, treat `main.rs` as a thin dispatch adapter and expose the core functionality as a library crate in `lib.rs`:

```text
mycli/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── main.rs         # CLI argument parsing, logging setup, exit code dispatch
│   ├── lib.rs          # Re-exports domain modules; testable without binary execution
│   ├── cli.rs          # clap structs, argument validators, flags
│   ├── config.rs       # TOML/JSON config loading and defaults
│   ├── core/           # Core domain logic, models, algorithms
│   └── commands/       # Implementation handlers for each CLI subcommand
│       ├── mod.rs
│       ├── build.rs
│       └── deploy.rs
└── tests/
    └── cli_tests.rs    # Integration tests using assert_cmd
```

## Writing a Clean `main.rs` Dispatcher

```rust
// src/main.rs
use anyhow::Result;
use clap::Parser;
use std::process::ExitCode;

mod cli;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args = cli::Cli::parse();

    // Initialize structured logging
    tracing_subscriber::fmt::init();

    if let Err(err) = run(args) {
        eprintln!("{:#}", err);
        return ExitCode::FAILURE;
    }

    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}

fn run(args: cli::Cli) -> Result<()> {
    match args.command {
        cli::Commands::Scan(opts) => mycli::scan(opts)?,
        cli::Commands::Build(opts) => mycli::build(opts)?,
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

## Benefits of the Dual-Target Layout

1. **Unit and Integration Testing:** Internal business logic functions can be unit-tested directly in `lib.rs` without spawning subprocesses.
2. **Reusability:** Other tools, benchmarks, or web services can import your crate as an internal dependency.
3. **Clean Architecture:** Changes to CLI argument flags or help text don't alter the underlying computational algorithms.
